summary: Held overnight in Split by a ferry crew strike on the way home
story: Our ferry from Split to Ancona on September 13 was due to leave at 20:00 and left at 09:00 the next morning because the crew went on strike. To be honest, the strike had been in the local news for a couple of weeks before we flew out, but we hoped it would be settled. We stayed at a hotel near the port, ate at the quay and took taxis. We paid cash for the meals and have no receipts for them. We also lost our first night's hotel in Bologna, which we had already paid for.

documents.content: Adria Lines. Sailing AL 212 Split to Ancona, scheduled September 13, 2026 at 20:00, departed September 14 at 09:00 because of a strike by the crew. The crew union served strike notice on August 18, 2026. Passengers: Owen Castell and Mara Castell. Under our passenger care policy, an overnight accommodation allowance of $40.00 per listed passenger, $80.00 in total, was refunded to the booking card on September 16, 2026.

documents.name: Receipts
documents.content: Hotel Marjan, September 13 to 14, one room: $410.00. Taxis, receipts 8841 and 8842: $18.00 and $18.00. Hotel Torre, Bologna, no-show September 14: $140.00.

decision.reason: The carrier confirms a 13 hour delay caused by a strike, longer than the 6 hour waiting period on Premium. The strike notice was served on August 18, 2026, after the policy was bought on May 12, 2026, so the strike was not publicly known when the policy was bought and the section 9 exclusion does not apply. The hotel is paid at the $350 a night limit for one room for two travelers. There are no meal receipts, so meals are paid at the flat $35 per traveler for one period of 24 hours or part of it, which is $70.00. Both taxis have receipts and are paid at $36.00. The prepaid night in Bologna is a consequential loss under section 9 and is left out. The eligible total is $456.00. Adria Lines refunded an accommodation allowance of $80.00, and that comes off under section 10, leaving $376.00. This is inside the $800 maximum, and Trip Delay has no deductible.
decision.policy_reference: Policy wording, sections 3, 9 and 10; claims manual, reasonable accommodation, consequential losses and meals without receipts

summary: Both passports lost on the way to the cruise port, replaced at the port passport agency on embarkation day
story: We drove down from Columbus to Port Calder for our Seabright cruise and stayed the night near the terminal. I had checked the travel folder with both passports before we left home and put it in my backpack. When we unpacked at the hotel that night the folder was gone. We think it slipped out at one of the rest stops along the highway. We called the rest stops and the highway patrol, but nobody had handed it in. First thing on embarkation morning we took a taxi to the passport agency in town, got photos done across the street and applied for emergency passports. They were ready before lunch, we took a taxi back to the hotel for our bags and we made it on board before the ship sailed. I am claiming the passport fees, the photos and the taxis.

The replacement costs were all paid on August 20, but the loss itself happened outside the trip dates, and section 9 excludes anything that happens outside the dates of the covered trip, so nothing is payable.

summary: Sprained ankle and cut knee on a river trip in Costa Rica, treated at a local hospital
story: We had a wild river day on June 10. It was a family float trip with local guides on the Lantern Run near La Fortuna. Near the end we stopped on a gravel bar for a swim. When I climbed back into the raft my foot slid on the rocks and my left ankle twisted under me. I also cut my knee open on the edge of a rock. The guides wrapped my ankle and drove me to the hospital in La Fortuna. They X-rayed the ankle, said it was a bad sprain and not broken, and put four stitches in my knee. They gave me a brace and crutches and I hobbled through the rest of the vacation. The doctor said I should get physio once I was back home, so I did four sessions in Tucson. I'm attaching the hospital bill, the hospital notes and the physio receipt. I'm claiming all of it.

decision.reason: The ankle sprain and knee cut were a sudden injury during the covered trip. Lantern Run is a family rafting trip with grade 2 rapids from start to finish, so it is not white-water rafting above grade 3 and the Adventure Sports add-on is not needed. The hospital record shows no earlier problem with the ankle or knee, and the itemized bill and records are on file, so the hospital charges of $955.00 are covered. The $340.00 of physiotherapy in Tucson was follow-up care after the customer got home, so it is not covered. The Economy deductible of $100.00 comes off, leaving a payout of $855.00, which is under the $25,000 maximum and needs no sign-off.

summary: Disc pain and sciatica needing an emergency admission in Santiago
story: On August 6 I woke in my hotel in Santiago with severe pain down my left leg and could not stand. The hotel called an ambulance and I was admitted overnight and had an MRI. They told me it was a herniated disc. I saw my doctor once back in April about my back, and I have not had an appointment since. Once I got home I had four physiotherapy sessions, which I have also listed. I have attached everything the hospital gave me.

items.description: Emergency department assessment
MRI scan
Orthopedic consultation
Medication dispensed
Overnight observation
Four physiotherapy sessions at home after the trip

documents.name: Hospital discharge summary
documents.content: Clinica Santa Maria, Santiago. Patient: Helen Park. Admitted August 6, 2026, 07:40, discharged August 7, 2026, 11:15. Presenting complaint: acute left leg pain, unable to bear weight. Examination: positive straight leg raise on the left, reduced ankle reflex. MRI lumbar spine: L5-S1 disc herniation compressing the left S1 nerve root. Diagnosis: lumbar disc herniation with left sciatica. Treatment: analgesia, observation overnight, orthopedic review. Medication reconciliation on admission, from the patient's US pharmacy record: multivitamin daily; cetirizine 10 mg as needed; naproxen 500 mg twice daily, increased from 250 mg twice daily by the prescriber on May 7, 2026, after a patient portal message reporting continuing back pain. Plan: discharge with analgesia, avoid flying for 48 hours, follow up with own physician at home.

documents.name: Letter from home physician
documents.content: Northlake Family Medicine, Seattle. To whom it may concern: Ms. Park was seen in clinic on April 10, 2026, for a lower back strain after lifting. Naproxen 250 mg twice daily was prescribed. She has had no further office visits with this practice.

documents.name: Itemized bill
documents.content: Clinica Santa Maria. Emergency assessment $540.00; MRI $1,180.00; orthopedic consultation $320.00; medication $46.50; overnight observation $610.00. Total $2,696.50, paid by card August 7, 2026.

documents.name: Home physiotherapy receipts
documents.content: Fremont Physical Therapy, Seattle. Four sessions, August 17 to 23, 2026: $180.00.

decision.reason: The policy was bought on July 3, so the 60-day look-back runs from May 4 to July 3. The April 10 clinic visit falls outside that window. However, the hospital's medication reconciliation shows that the customer's prescriber increased her naproxen from 250 mg to 500 mg twice daily on May 7 for continuing back pain, which is inside the window, and a change in dose is a change in medication. The back condition is therefore pre-existing, the policy has no Pre-Existing Condition Waiver, and section 7 excludes the claim. The home physiotherapy would also be excluded as treatment after returning home.
decision.policy_reference: Policy wording, section 7; claims manual, pre-existing conditions

summary: Couple cancelled a week in Cancun, Mexico after the airline stopped all flights to Cancun ahead of a hurricane
story: My wife and I were booked to fly to Cancun on August 21 for a week at the beach. On August 20 Skylark Airways emailed to say every flight to Cancun was cancelled because of the hurricane, and nothing would fly there for days. There was no way to get there, so we cancelled the trip. The airline would not give us anything back because we were on their basic fare, and the hotel only refunded part of what we paid. Altogether we are out a lot of money for a vacation we never got to take. We have kept every email and receipt, and they are all attached.

Seven nights at Hotel Arena Turquesa, Cancun, prepaid

documents.content: Booking SK4R8M for Harold Wrenfield and Diane Wrenfield. Flight SK1187 Columbus to Cancun, August 21, 2026, returning SK1188 August 28, 2026. Fare paid by card: $1,180.00, fare type Basic. Notice issued August 20, 2026: Skylark Airways has suspended all service to and from Cancun International Airport from August 20 through August 23, 2026. The suspension follows the National Hurricane Center advisory of 11:00 a.m. EDT on August 18, 2026, which named Tropical Storm Tobias and forecast its arrival on the Cancun coast on August 21, and the storm's upgrade to a hurricane on August 20. Customers on Basic fares who choose not to rebook are not eligible for a refund or a travel credit. The passengers did not rebook, and the booking was cancelled on August 20, 2026.

documents.content: Reservation for Mr and Mrs Wrenfield, August 21 to August 28, 2026, ocean-view double room, prepaid rate, $1,260.00 charged on July 5, 2026. documents.content: Visa ending 3318. July 2, 2026: Skylark Airways $1,180.00. July 5, 2026: Hotel Arena Turquesa $1,260.00. August 24, 2026: Hotel Arena Turquesa refund -$520.00.

documents.name: National Hurricane Center advisory
documents.content: National Hurricane Center, August 18, 2026: Tropical Storm Tobias has formed in the western Caribbean. It is expected to become a hurricane and to reach the coast of the Yucatan Peninsula near Cancun on August 21.

decision.reason: Section 9 says no benefit pays for events that were publicly known before you bought the policy, such as a named storm. The airline's notice shows that Tropical Storm Tobias was named and forecast to reach Cancun on August 18, 2026, and the policy was bought on August 19, 2026. The storm was therefore publicly known before purchase. The flight suspension would otherwise be a covered reason under section 2, but this exclusion applies to every benefit, so the unrefunded flight and hotel costs are not payable.
decision.policy_reference: Policy wording, section 9 (events publicly known before purchase) and section 2; claims manual, sections 2 and 4

calculation.step: Cancellation caused by Tropical Storm Tobias, named and forecast on August 18, 2026, the day before the policy was bought on August 19, 2026: excluded under section 9

summary: Cabin bag snatched at Valencia train station on the last day of the trip
story: On September 12, the day I was due to fly home, I was standing at the ticket machines in the main train station in Valencia with my cabin bag on my shoulder. A man on a scooter rode past, grabbed the strap and pulled it off me, and he was gone before I could do anything. I had packed my gadgets in that bag so they would not go in the hold, along with a couple of t-shirts. I went straight to the police office in the station and made a report. I flew home that evening as planned. I am claiming for everything that was in the bag.

summary: Backpack stolen from a locked rental car at a fuel station
story: On September 8 I stopped for fuel at a station outside Impruneta. I locked the rental car and went inside to pay. I was gone maybe five minutes. When I came back the car had been broken into and my backpack was gone. It had my passport, my laptop, some cash and some clothes in it. The station attendant helped me call the police and I made a report straight away. I also told the rental company, because the rental came with some cover for belongings, and they have since settled part of it. The next day I took a taxi to the US Consulate in Florence, had new passport photos taken and paid for an emergency passport so I could fly home. I am claiming for everything I lost and what the passport cost me.

At about 10:50 the reporting person left a locked rental car, a grey hatchback, at the Carburanti Vallebruna fuel station to pay inside. On returning he found the rear hatch lock forced and the parcel shelf cover pulled back. A backpack that had been in the closed luggage compartment under the cover was missing. Reported contents: US passport, laptop computer, about $90 in cash, a jacket, two shirts. No suspects identified.

decision.reason: The police report shows the backpack was locked in the closed luggage compartment under the parcel shelf cover and out of sight, so it was attended under section 5 and the manual's vehicles note, and the theft was reported to the police within 24 hours. On Premium with no Electronics Plus, the laptop counts at the $300 per-item limit. The cash of $90 is under the $100 cash limit, and the jacket at $140 and the shirts at $90 are under the limit, giving $620. The rental company's $200 settlement for the laptop comes off next, leaving $420. The $50 Premium deductible then leaves $370 under Baggage and Personal Effects. Separately, section 6 pays the emergency passport fee of $160, photos of $15 and taxi to the consulate of $44, totalling $219. That is within the $250 maximum and carries no deductible. The total payout is $589.

summary: Passport found missing at passport control on arrival in Barcelona; emergency passport obtained at the consulate
story: I flew into Barcelona on August 4 to join a cruise. At passport control I opened my travel wallet and my passport was not there. I think it slipped out on the plane or at the gate, but the airline never found it. The officers let me in so I could go to the consulate. The next morning I had new photos taken, took a taxi to the consulate and paid for an emergency passport, which I got that afternoon. Because I spent the whole day there I missed the Montserrat day trip I had paid for in advance through the cruise line, and they would not refund it. I am claiming the consulate fee, the photos, the taxi and the trip I missed.

documents.content: I arrived on flight NV 2214 at Barcelona on August 4, 2026 at 18:40. At passport control I found my passport was missing from my travel wallet. decision.reason: The passport was lost during the covered trip, and the consulate fee ($95.00), the photos ($12.00) and the taxi to the consulate ($38.00) are receipted. These are exactly what the passport benefit pays, and no deductible applies. The missed Montserrat excursion followed indirectly from the lost passport, so it is a consequential loss and is excluded. The eligible total of $145.00 is inside the $150 Economy maximum for passport and travel documents, so $145.00 is paid. The customer has two earlier claims. The baggage claim filed on 2025-08-02 falls outside the 12 months before this claim was filed on 2026-08-10, so only the trip delay claim filed on 2025-12-14 counts. This is the customer's second claim in 12 months, not the third, and it is decided in the normal way.
